name: Rovaniemi Art Museum (Korundi House of Culture)
funding: A municipal museum of the City of Rovaniemi: EUR 1.76M spent in 2025, EUR 310,218 from the state. Its core is the Wihuri Foundation's collection of nearly 4,000 works, given in 1983.
watch: The Jenny and Antti Wihuri Foundation still adds about 60 works a year to the collection the city shows.
records_note: Figures are in the Finnish Heritage Agency's museum statistics; the museum names the donor of its collection.

name: Särestöniemi Museum (Särestöniemi-museo)
funding: A foundation-owned museum. Of EUR 660,917 income in 2025, admissions gave EUR 295,853, sales EUR 166,929, state museum funding EUR 127,335 and sponsors EUR 70,800.
watch: The statistics do not name the sponsors behind EUR 70,800 in 2025.
records_note: Figures are in the Finnish Heritage Agency's museum statistics; no sponsor list was found.

name: KADIST
funding: Privately funded by a French family, Mission Local reported on 3 September 2025; its Americas director said the closing of its San Francisco space that month had nothing to do with funding. Its own site names no funder: it lists co-founders Vincent Worms (president) and Sandra Terdjman (vice-president) and says it operates through the endowment fund AKAT – KADIST in France and two US 501(c)(3) entities, Artnow International Inc and KADIST Collection Manager Inc. Their Form 990-PF returns, as shown on ProPublica's Nonprofit Explorer: Artnow International, year to December 2024, revenue USD 1.42M, nearly all of it contributions, expenses USD 1.46M, Vincent Worms chairman; KADIST Collection Manager, total assets USD 41.6M at December 2024, after contributions of USD 44.7M in 2023. The pages read did not name the contributors.
watch: A non-profit contemporary art organisation with a collection its site puts at over 2,600 works by 1,400 artists; it runs exhibitions, residencies and loans to museums. The collection was started in 2001 and the Paris space opened in 2006 (Wikipedia). A second space at 3295 20th Street in San Francisco's Mission District, opened in 2011, closed on 6 September 2025 after 14 years; the director said the work had shifted to international collaborations and that no one would be laid off (Mission Local).
records_note: Two US entities file Form 990-PF, readable on ProPublica's Nonprofit Explorer; the pages read did not show accounts for the French endowment fund.

name: Palais de la Porte Dorée (Musée national de l'histoire de l'immigration)
funding: Run by a public body under four ministries (integration, culture, education and research), formed in 2012 by merging the Cité nationale de l'histoire de l'immigration with the Aquarium.
watch: The immigration exhibition opened in October 2007 and was reinstalled in June 2023 after a three year closure, in Albert Laprade's 1931 Art Deco palace.

propaganda.summary: Built 1928 to 1931 as the Musée des Colonies for the Paris Colonial Exhibition, the palace was a propaganda work made to promote the benefits of colonisation and the merits of the French empire.

name: Joseph Stalin Museum
funding: A Georgian state museum, funded by the Ministry of Culture and Monuments and listed as a heritage monument; restoration tenders run through the State Procurement Agency. Lia Okroperidze is director.
watch: The 1957 complex by Archil Kurdiani holds about 40,000 items; Gori counted roughly 162,000 visitors in 2018. A room on repressions was added in 2010.

propaganda.summary: Soviet authorities opened the museum complex in 1957, a year after Khrushchev's secret speech, as a monument honouring Stalin; a 2012 Georgian plan to refocus it on his atrocities was never carried out.

name: Deutsches Hygiene-Museum
funding: Run by the Stiftung Deutsches Hygiene-Museum, a non-profit foundation funded by matching annual contributions from Saxony and the City of Dresden, with further grants from federal bodies, businesses and foundations.
watch: Founded 1912 by Odol manufacturer Karl August Lingner. Dresden mayor Annekatrin Klepsch chairs its trustees and Iris Edenheiser has directed it since 2022.

propaganda.summary: From 1933 the museum served Nazi racial ideology as a propaganda machine of racial hygiene, co-producing with NSDAP offices the touring exhibitions Blut und Rasse (1935 to 1938) and Ewiges Volk (1937 to 1939).

name: Haus der Kunst
funding: The Free State of Bavaria and the Friends of Haus der Kunst are shareholders. The Alexander Tutsek Foundation is the major supporter. The Kai and Beisheim foundations also give.
watch: A Bavarian ministry official chairs its supervisory board. 2024 attendance was nearly 440,000.

propaganda.summary: Hitler had the building erected and opened it on 18 July 1937 for the annual Great German Art Exhibitions, held to 1944. His photographer Heinrich Hoffmann took charge of selecting works, and Hitler decided finally.

name: Museum für Deutsche Geschichte
funding: Closed 1990. The GDR state owned it and the last GDR government's Council of Ministers dissolved it. Its holdings and the Zeughaus passed to the Deutsches Historisches Museum.
watch: The Zeughaus on Unter den Linden now houses the Deutsches Historisches Museum.

propaganda.summary: The SED Politburo decided in 1950 to found the GDR's central history museum, and the Central Committee approved its staff. It presented a Marxist-Leninist view of history that legitimised the GDR until 1990.

name: Ilulissat Art Museum (Ilulissat Kunstmuseum)
funding: One of Greenland's two small municipal art museums, in Avannaata Municipality, set up in 1995 in the 1923 colony manager's house.
watch: Built on a collection of Emanuel A. Petersen's paintings; it runs an artist residency.
records_note: No budget, board or accounts found.

name: Ilulissat Icefjord Centre (Kangiata Illorsua)
funding: Built by a partnership of the Danish foundation Realdania, Avannaata Municipality and the Government of Greenland. The Nordea Foundation, Augustinus Fonden, Bloomberg Philanthropies and the Oak Foundation paid for the exhibition.
watch: A climate visitor centre by Dorte Mandrup at the UNESCO Icefjord; one exhibition funder's money comes from tobacco.
records_note: No accounts or operating budget found; its site did not answer on 17 Nov 2026.
